evidence: app/eventyay/base/services/announcement.py: async service functions return serialize_public() dicts directly — the translation from model to dict happens inside the service, which is appropriate single-location boundary translation.

app/eventyay/base/models/access_code.py: send_invite() performs a lazy import of QueuedMail inside the method to avoid circular imports — this is a seam smell indicating the model has outgrown its package boundary.

app/eventyay/base/payment.py imports from eventyay.presale.views (get_cart, get_cart_total, cart_session, get_or_create_cart_id) — a base-layer module depending on a view-layer module is an inverted boundary that forces view logic into base package tests.
app/eventyay/base/services/cart.py imports from eventyay.base.services.checkin._save_answers — private symbol crossing service boundary without a clean contract.

app/eventyay/presale/utils.py: _event_view wrapper and _detect_event integrate middleware (LocaleMiddleware(NotImplementedError)) with domain routing — LocaleMiddleware is instantiated with a NotImplementedError as its get_response argument (a sentinel hack rather than clean composition).
app/eventyay/base/services/orders.py imports from 20+ modules including models, services, signals, and API models (OAuthApplication) — a hub service with wide import fan-in.

app/eventyay/base/models/event.py imports from eventyay.talk_rules.event (can_change_event_settings, etc.) and eventyay.eventyay_common.video.permissions — model layer importing from business-rule and video-permission layers.
app/eventyay/control/views/orders.py imports vat_moss.id, a VAT computation library, directly in the view layer — VAT logic belongs in the service layer for testability.
app/eventyay/base/models/__init__.py re-exports 100+ symbols, making the model boundary extremely wide and all callers tightly coupled to its completeness.
app/eventyay/base/services/checkin.py: get_logic_environment() returns a Logic object populated locally — clean explicit output from the function with no hidden state.
app/eventyay/common/views/cache.py: conditional_cache_page delegates cleanly to etag_cache_page — good composition without back-and-forth.
app/eventyay/orga/views/review.py: ReviewDashboard inherits from both EventPermissionRequired and BaseSubmissionList, composing permission and query logic cleanly.

strengths: Announcement service translates to dict at the boundary (serialize_public) in a single, obvious place.
get_logic_environment() returns an explicit Logic object — no hidden state mutation across the service boundary.
conditional_cache_page -> etag_cache_page is a clean one-direction delegation with explicit parameters.
EventPermissionRequiredMixin and EventPermissionMiddleware both centralize auth enforcement at the boundary rather than scattering it in handlers.
BaseSubmissionList / ReviewDashboard mixin composition is coherent — each mixin owns a distinct concern.
mid_level_elegance.issue_character: The dominant pattern is layer boundary violations: base.payment importing presale.views, event model importing business-rule and video permission layers, and a 20+ import hub in services/orders.py that makes the service layer's seam unclear.
mid_level_elegance.score_rationale: The codebase shows genuine effort at service-layer decomposition (announcement, checkin, cart, orders as separate services), but the boundary integrity is repeatedly violated by upward imports (base -> presale, model -> business-rule layer) and a lazy-import hack in access_code.py that signals an unresolved circular dependency. The services/orders.py import fan-in (20+ modules including API models) creates a hub that makes the service-layer seam difficult to test or extend. These are mid-level seam problems — not naming or internal implementation issues — and they affect a significant fraction of core paths, warranting a score in the upper-50s.

issues.summary: base/payment.py imports view-layer symbols from presale.views, inverting the layer boundary
issues.suggestion: Move get_cart, get_cart_total, cart_session, get_or_create_cart_id to eventyay.base.services.cart so both base.payment and presale.views can import from the service layer without crossing the boundary.

issues.summary: base/models/event.py imports from talk_rules.event and eventyay_common.video.permissions, pulling business rules into the model layer
evidence: from eventyay.talk_rules.event import (can_change_event_settings, can_create_events, has_any_permission, is_event_visible,)
issues.suggestion: Invert the dependency: have talk_rules and video.permissions reference the model through explicit model imports, not the reverse. Use rules model permissions (rules_permissions on Meta) that reference callables from the model file itself, or move permission callables into the model module.

issues.summary: SubmitterAccessCode.send_invite() uses lazy import of QueuedMail to avoid circular dependency — signals unresolved boundary
evidence: def send_invite(self, to, subject, text): from eventyay.base.models import QueuedMail
issues.suggestion: Extract send_invite into an access_code service module that imports both SubmitterAccessCode and QueuedMail at module level, removing the circular dependency by placing the orchestration outside the model.

issues.summary: LocaleMiddleware instantiated with NotImplementedError as get_response sentinel in _detect_event
evidence: LocaleMiddleware(NotImplementedError).process_request(request)  — passing an exception class as the get_response argument
issues.suggestion: Either extract locale processing into a standalone function (avoid middleware instantiation entirely) or use a no-op lambda as the get_response argument to be explicit about the intent.

issues.summary: base/services/orders.py imports from 20+ modules including OAuthApplication — excessive fan-in blurs service seam
evidence: Imports include: base.models (12 models), base.models.event, base.models.orders, base.models.organizer, base.models.product, base.models.tax, base.payment, base.services (invoices, locking, mail, pricing, quotas, tasks, tickets), base.signals, api.models.OAuthApplication
issues.suggestion: Split the orders service into focused sub-services: order_creation.py, order_cancellation.py, order_payment.py. The OAuthApplication import specifically suggests API concerns leaking into the core service — move that logic to the API layer.

root_causes: Merger of pretix (ticketing) and pretalx (talk management) codebases brought two independently designed layer models that were not fully reconciled at the boundary level
The base model layer accumulated business rules incrementally rather than keeping rules in a dedicated layer
likely_symptoms: access_code_lazy_import — symptom of circular dependency from cross-layer coupling
locale_middleware_sentinel — symptom of middleware being co-opted for non-middleware use
possible_false_positives: base/models/__init__.py wide re-export — intentional package facade for stable import paths, justified but creates a wide surface
